work: Enarratio in Epistolam II B. Pauli ad Thessalonicenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: EXPOSITIO PRIMI CAPITULI : PAULUS ET SILVANUS ET TIMOTHEUS ECCLESIÆ THESSALONICENSIUM.
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians.

paras.t: PAULUS et Silvanus et Timotheus, Ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium, in Deo Patre nostro et Domino Jesu Christo, etc. Omnia verba hæc in exordio epistolæ præcedentis exposita sunt. Nam et verbo et sensu idem est utriusque epistolæ principium.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul and Sylvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians. In God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ|PAULUS et Silvanus et Timotheus, Ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium, in Deo Patre nostro et Domino Jesu Christo]], etc. All these words have been expounded at the opening of the preceding epistle[[1 Thess 1:1||]]. For the beginning of both epistles is the same, in word and in sense.

paras.t: Gratias agere debemus Deo semper, id est omni tempore congruenti, pro vobis, id est propter beneficia vobis divinitus præstita, o fratres : ad hoc enim tenemur tanquam pastores vestri. Caritas quoque qua de vestra salute gaudemus et Dei honorem concupimus, ad hanc nos gratiarum actionem constringit. Ita ut dignum est, id est multum affectuose atque humiliter, sicut pro tantis beneficiis, tanto benefactori a tantillis gratias agi decet. Quoniam supercrescit, id est, plurimum proficit, fides vestra : nam per illuminationem Spiritus Sancti fit clarior, atque per opera bona vivacior ; et abundat caritas uniuscujusque vestrum in invicem, id est, unusquisque vestrum alium amat ferventer spirituali et sancta dilectione :
paras.en: [[1:3|We are bound to give thanks always to God|Gratias agere debemus Deo semper]], that is, at every fitting time, [[1:3|for you|pro vobis]], that is, on account of the benefits divinely bestowed on you, O [[1:3|brethren|fratres]]: for to this we are bound as your shepherds. The charity too, by which we rejoice in your salvation and long for God's honour, constrains us to this thanksgiving. [[1:3|as it is fitting|Ita ut dignum est]], that is, with great affection and humility, as it is fitting that thanks be given by such little ones to so great a benefactor for such great benefits. [[1:3|because your faith groweth exceedingly|quoniam supercrescit fides vestra]], that is, makes very great progress: for by the illumination of the Holy Ghost it becomes clearer, and by good works more lively; [[1:3|and the charity of every one of you towards each other aboundeth|et abundat caritas uniuscujusque vestrum in invicem]], that is, each one of you loves the other fervently with a spiritual and holy love:

paras.t: ita ut et nos ipsi in vobis, id est de vestra perfectione, vel in perfectionis vestræ consideratione, gloriemur in Ecclesiis Dei, id est coram congregationibus Christianorum, ad quorum ædificationem lætanter referimus vestras virtutes : gloriemur, inquam, pro, id est de, patientia vestra et fide, quæ fortiter conservastis in omnibus persecutionibus vestris, quæ extrinsecus infliguntur, et tribulationibus aliis, quas sustinetis, in exemplum, id est in declarationem, justi judicii Dei futuri in morte cujuslibet, vel in die novissimo. Tribulationes quippe quas sustinetis, testantur et manifestant quod Deus post hanc vitam judicat patientes et inferentes, reddens singulis quod merentur, videlicet patientibus gloriam. Qui enim humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria. Quum namque cernamus in hac vita impios prosperari et justos opprimere, justos autem adversitatibus fatigari et opprimi etiam usque ad mortem, oportet concedere quod justus et sapiens Deus post hanc vitam omnia recte disponat, juste judicet, et optime ordinet : quod non fit nisi per justam damnationem malorum et beatificationem justorum. Ut digni, id est gloriosi, habeamini (vel, Digni habeamini, id est, digni sitis per opera sancta recipi) in regno Dei, id est Ecclesia triumphanti ac throno cœlesti, pro quo, videlicet ut sic digni habeamini, et patimini tanta adversa, pensantes illud Evangelii : Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, ecce enim merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Si enim compatimur, et conregnabimus.
paras.en: [[1:4|So that we ourselves also glory in you|ita ut et nos ipsi in vobis]], that is, of your perfection, or in considering your perfection, [[1:4|glory in you in the churches of God|gloriemur in Ecclesiis Dei]], that is, before the congregations of Christians, to whose edification we joyfully report your virtues: we glory, I say, [[1:4|for|pro]], that is, about, [[1:4|your patience and faith|patientia vestra et fide]], which you have bravely kept [[1:4|in all your persecutions|in omnibus persecutionibus vestris]], which are inflicted from without, [[1:4|and tribulations|et tribulationibus]] of other kinds, [[1:4|which you endure|quas sustinetis]], [[1:5|For an example|in exemplum]], that is, for a declaration, [[1:5|of the just judgment of God|justi judicii Dei]] to come at each one's death, or on the last day. For the tribulations you endure testify and make plain that God, after this life, judges those who suffer and those who inflict, rendering to each what he deserves, namely glory to those who suffer. For he that hath been humbled shall be in glory[[Job 22:29||]] [no margin reference is printed; the words are those of Job 22:29]. For since we see in this life the wicked prospering and oppressing the just, and the just wearied by adversities and oppressed even unto death, we must grant that the just and wise God after this life disposes all things rightly, judges justly and orders them most well: which comes about only through the just damnation of the wicked and the beatification of the just. [[1:5|that you may be counted worthy|ut digni habeamini]] [Denis's text reads *habeamini*, “we may be counted”], that is, glorious (or, “be counted worthy”, that is, be worthy through holy works to be received) [[1:5|of the kingdom of God|in regno Dei]], that is, into the Church triumphant and the heavenly throne, [[1:5|for which|pro quo]], namely that you may thus be counted worthy, [[1:5|also you suffer|et patimini]] such great adversities, weighing that word of the Gospel: [[Luke 6:23|Be glad in that day and rejoice: for behold, your reward is great in heaven|Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, ecce enim merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]][[Matt 5:12||]]. For if we suffer with him, we shall also reign with him[[Rom 8:17||]][[2 Tim 2:12||]].

paras.t: Si tamen, id est quia, justum est apud Deum, id est, in mente divina hoc justum censetur, retribuere tribulationem his qui vos tribulant, id est persecutoribus vestris debitas reddere pœnas pro pœnis quas vobis infligunt. Quod utique justum est et continget, sicut et Psalmista testatur : Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum, facit judicium injuriam patientibus. Unde et in Job habetur : Deus inultum abire non patitur. Justum quoque est apud Deum, et vobis qui tribulamini propter justitiam, requiem dare æternam nobiscum in patria. Ideo namque in libro Sapientiæ legimus : Deus tentavit illos, et invenit illos dignos se; ideoque accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini. Et in Apocalypsi : Isti sunt qui venerunt de tribulatione magna, ideo sunt ante thronum Dei.
paras.en: [[1:6|Seeing|Si tamen]], that is, because, [[1:6|it is a just thing with God|justum est apud Deum]], that is, in the divine mind this is judged just, [[1:6|to repay tribulation to them that trouble you|retribuere tribulationem his qui vos tribulant]], that is, to render to your persecutors the penalties due for the pains they inflict on you. Which surely is just and will come to pass, as the Psalmist also testifies: [[Ps 145:7|Who keepeth truth for ever: who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong|Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum, facit judicium injuriam patientibus]] [the Douay-Rheims divides this between Ps 145:6 and 7]. Hence in Job too it is said: God doth not suffer it to go unrevenged[[Job 24:12||]]. It is just also with God [[1:7|And to you who are troubled|et vobis qui tribulamini]] for justice' sake, to give [[1:7|rest|requiem]] eternal [[1:7|with us|nobiscum]] in the fatherland. For this reason we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 3:5|God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself|Deus tentavit illos, et invenit illos dignos se]]; [[Wis 5:17|Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord|ideoque accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini]]. And in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 7:14|These are they who are come out of great tribulation|Isti sunt qui venerunt de tribulatione magna]], therefore they are before the throne of God[[Apoc 7:15||]] [the margin gives Apoc. vii, 14, 15].

paras.t: Hæc autem retributio plenarie fiet, et justum est apud Deum eam compleri, in revelatione, id est manifesta apparitione, Domini Jesu venientis de cœlo in die novissimo, cum angelis virtutis ejus, id est angelis sanctis suæ divinæ potestati, imo et suæ humanitati subjectis ; in flamma ignis dantis vindictam, id est in revelatione Jesu dantis in flamma ignis, id est per ignem flammantem, vindictam, id est justam ultionem, iis qui non noverunt Deum scientia formata quæ facit quod novit agendum, id est injustis, qui etsi dicant se nosse Deum, factis negant. De hac enim scientia ait Joannes in prima sua Canonica : Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est. Vel per ignorantes Deum, intelliguntur idololatræ. Et iis qui non obediunt Evangelio, id est evangelicæ doctrinæ, Domini nostri Jesu Christi. De hac Christi revelatione et flamma ignis psaltes David clarissime prophetavit : Deus manifeste veniet, Deus noster, et non silebit ; ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet.
paras.en: Now this retribution will be made in full, and it is just with God that it be fulfilled, [[1:7|when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed|in revelatione Domini Jesu]], that is, at the manifest appearing of the Lord Jesus, coming [[1:7|from heaven|de cœlo]] on the last day, [[1:7|with the angels of his power|cum angelis virtutis ejus]], that is, with the holy angels subject to his divine power, nay, to his humanity as well; [[1:8|In a flame of fire, giving vengeance|in flamma ignis dantis vindictam]], that is, at the revelation of Jesus giving in a flame of fire, that is, through flaming fire, vengeance, that is, just requital, [[1:8|to them who know not God|iis qui non noverunt Deum]] with formed knowledge [that is, knowledge informed by charity], which does what it knows ought to be done; that is, to the unjust, who though they say they know God, in their works deny him[[Tit 1:16||]]. For of this knowledge John says in his first Canonical epistle: [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est]]. Or by those ignorant of God are meant idolaters. [[1:8|and who obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ|Et iis qui non obediunt Evangelio, id est evangelicæ doctrinæ, Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, the gospel teaching. Of this revelation of Christ and flame of fire the psalmist David most clearly prophesied: [[Ps 49:3|God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, and shall not keep silence. A fire shall burn before him|Deus manifeste veniet, Deus noster, et non silebit ; ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet]].

paras.t: Qui nescientes et inobedientes, pœnas dabunt, id est persolvent et luent, in interitu æternas, id est æternaliter perdurantes, et quasi occidentes, non tamen exstinguentes, eos quos punient. Unde hæ pœnæ sunt mors secunda, æterna et amarissima. Has igitur pœnas dabunt, id est, sustinebunt sibi inflictas, a facie Domini, id est a præsentia Christi, qui dicet : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Cujus facies reprobis erit horrenda ac pœnalissima, ita ut dicant montibus et petris : Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie Sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni. Et a gloria virtutis ejus, id est ab excellentia seu majestate potentiæ Christi, qui in suo imperio reprobos in pœnas inferni detrudet. Data namque est ei omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra.
paras.en: [[1:9|Who|Qui]], ignorant and disobedient, [[1:9|shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction|pœnas dabunt, in interitu æternas]] [*pœnas dabunt*, literally “shall pay penalties”], that is, shall pay and atone, eternal punishments, that is, lasting eternally, and as it were slaying, yet not extinguishing, those whom they punish. Hence these punishments are the second death[[Apoc 21:8||]], eternal and most bitter. These punishments, then, they shall pay, that is, endure as inflicted on them, [[1:9|from the face of the Lord|a facie Domini]], that is, from the presence of Christ, who will say: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. His face will be dreadful and most painful to the reprobate, so that they will say to the mountains and the rocks: [[Apoc 6:16|Fall upon us and hide us from the face of him that sitteth upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb|Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie Sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni]]. [[1:9|and from the glory of his power|Et a gloria virtutis ejus]], that is, from the excellence or majesty of the might of Christ, who by his command will thrust the reprobate down into the pains of hell. For [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]] has been given to him.

paras.t: Quum venerit Christus glorificari, id est glorificatus atque magnificus apparere, in Sanctis suis, id est in præmiatione seu glorificatione electorum suorum ; et quum venerit admirabilis fieri in cordibus omnium intuentium in omnibus qui crediderunt, id est in justa retributione seu præmio universorum fidelium, bonos salvando, impiosque damnando. Ex quo effectu cunctis patebit quam admirabilis sit Dominus Jesus, quemadmodum scriptum est : Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis. Signum vero quod omnia ista sic fient, est : Quia creditum est testimonium nostrum, id est, attestatio seu prædicatio nostra de justo judicio Dei credita est, super vos, id est a vobis vel in cordibus vestris. Hoc enim sensu in Isaia habetur : Spiritus Domini super me, id est in me. Creditum est in die illo, id est, sic quod complebitur in die novissimo, quando omnes simul remunerabuntur ; vel, In die illo, id est de die illo, quia de die judicii credidistis quæ prædicavimus vobis.
paras.en: [[1:10|When he shall come to be glorified|Quum venerit Christus glorificari]], Christ, that is, to appear glorified and magnificent, [[1:10|in his saints|in Sanctis suis]], that is, in the rewarding or glorifying of his elect; and when he shall come [[1:10|to be made wonderful|admirabilis fieri]] in the hearts of all who behold, [[1:10|in all them who have believed|in omnibus qui crediderunt]], that is, in the just requital or reward of all the faithful, saving the good and damning the wicked. From which effect it will be plain to all how wonderful the Lord Jesus is, as it is written: [[Ps 67:36|God is wonderful in his saints|Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis]]. And the sign that all these things will so come to pass is this: [[1:10|because our testimony was believed|Quia creditum est testimonium nostrum]], that is, our attestation or preaching about the just judgment of God has been believed, [[1:10|upon you|super vos]], that is, by you, or in your hearts. For in this sense it is said in Isaias: [[Is 61:1|The spirit of the Lord is upon me|Spiritus Domini super me]], that is, in me. It was believed [[1:10|in that day|in die illo]], that is, in such wise that it will be fulfilled on the last day, when all will be rewarded together; or, “in that day”, that is, about that day, because you believed what we preached to you about the day of judgment.

paras.t: In quo negotio seu testimonio prædicationis nostræ, etiam oramus semper pro vobis, ut dignetur, id est, dignos efficiat, vos vocatione sua, id est beatitudine ad quam vocati estis, Deus noster, et impleat omnem voluntatem bonitatis suæ, id est, quidquid suæ pietati placitum est, ad effectum perducat in vobis, quatenus faciat vos suis præceptis atque consiliis misericorditer datis obedire in omnibus. Impleat quoque et opus fidei, id est opera virtuosa ex fide nascentia, sine quibus fides mortua est in se ipsa. Vel, opus fidei proprie intelligitur oris confessio, qua quis fidem profitetur. Corde enim creditur ad justitiam, ore vero confessio fit ad salutem. Quæ confessio summe necessaria fuit martyribus tempore Apostolorum, et postmodum diu. In virtute constantiæ seu animi firmitate, vel fortiter, stetis, atque in finem perseveretis.
paras.en: [[1:11|Wherefore|In quo]] [literally “in which”], that is, in which business or testimony of our preaching, [[1:11|also we pray always for you|etiam oramus semper pro vobis]], [[1:11|That our God would make you worthy|ut dignetur]], that is, may make you worthy, [[1:11|of his vocation|vos vocatione sua]], that is, of the beatitude to which you have been called, [[1:11|our God|Deus noster]], [[1:11|and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness|et impleat omnem voluntatem bonitatis suæ]], that is, may bring to effect in you whatever is pleasing to his kindness, so as to make you obey in all things his precepts and counsels mercifully given. May he fulfil also [[1:11|the work of faith|et opus fidei]], that is, the virtuous works born of faith, without which faith is dead in itself[[Jas 2:20||]]. Or, the work of faith is properly understood as the confession of the mouth by which one professes the faith. [[Rom 10:10|For, with the heart, we believe unto justice: but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Corde enim creditur ad justitiam, ore vero confessio fit ad salutem]]. This confession was supremely necessary for the martyrs in the time of the Apostles and for long afterwards. [[1:11|in power|In virtute]] of constancy, or firmness of soul, or bravely, that you may stand and persevere to the end.

paras.t: Ut clarificetur nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est, ipse Christus clarificetur, in vobis dupliciter : Primo, ut eum sincere cognoscatis, et digne honoretis. Sic enim clarificatur, id est, clare habetur, scitur et honoratur in cordibus vestris. De tali clarificatione ait Salvator : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Secundo, ut divina perfectio Christi in vobis appareat, et ita Christus in vobis per suum præclarum effectum innotescat seu declaretur. Et vos in illo, id est, in Christo clarificemini, videndo eum in patria facie ad faciem. Non ergo eodem modo clarificatur Christus in nobis, et nos in illo. Per hoc enim quod ipse clarificatur in nobis, nihil perfectionis aut gloriæ ei accrescit; per hoc autem quod nos clarificamur in Christo, summe perficimur. Sic igitur clarificemini in illo, secundum gratiam Dei nostri, id est juxta mensuram gratiæ vobis a sancta Trinitate exhibitæ, et Domini Jesu Christi, id est secundum eamdem gratiam, quæ nobis per Christum tanquam per mediatorem et causam meritoriam datur. Hoc dicit Apostolus, ne quis propriis meritis principaliter innitatur.
paras.en: [[1:12|That the name of our Lord Jesus|Ut clarificetur nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi]] [*clarificetur*, “be made bright, glorified”], that is, that Christ himself may be glorified, [[1:12|may be glorified in you|in vobis]] in two ways: first, that you may know him sincerely and honour him worthily. For so he is glorified, that is, is held clearly, known and honoured in your hearts. Of such glorification the Saviour says: [[John 17:1|said: the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. Secondly, that the divine perfection of Christ may appear in you, and so Christ may become known or be declared in you through his glorious effect. [[1:12|and you in him|Et vos in illo]], that is, that you may be glorified in Christ, seeing him in the fatherland face to face[[1 Cor 13:12||]]. Christ, then, is not glorified in us in the same way as we in him. For by his being glorified in us no perfection or glory accrues to him; but by our being glorified in Christ we are perfected in the highest degree. So then may you be glorified in him, [[1:12|according to the grace of our God|secundum gratiam Dei nostri]], that is, according to the measure of grace shown you by the holy Trinity, [[1:12|and of the Lord Jesus Christ|et Domini Jesu Christi]], that is, according to that same grace, which is given us through Christ as mediator and meritorious cause. The Apostle says this lest anyone rely principally on his own merits.
